questiontext.text:
The graph of \(y = {@base@}\) is mapped onto \(y = {@image@}\) by a translation. Give the translation vector.

([[input:ans1]] \(^\circ\))
[[input:ans2]]
[[validation:ans1]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt1]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Take out the \({@b@}\): \(y = {@fact@}\).

Replacing \(x\) by \(x {@tc(sh)@}^\circ\) moves the graph the opposite way to the sign, by the angle divided by \({@b@}\): \({@abs(sh)@}^\circ\) to the [[if test="is(sh > 0)"]]left[[else]]right[[/if]]. Adding \({@d@}\) outside moves every point {@updown@} by \({@abs(d)@}\).

The translation vector is \(\begin{pmatrix} {@hx@}^\circ \\ {@d@} \end{pmatrix}\).

questiondescription.text:
Trigonometry III: translation vector of a wave

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.5: Give the column vector of the translation mapping y = a sin bx (or cos) onto y = a sin(bx + c) + d.

Core

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="not princ"]]

Accepted. The wave repeats every \({@wper@}^\circ\), so your shift of \({@ans1@}^\circ\) gives the same graph as the shortest shift, \({@hx@}^\circ\).

[[/if]]

You moved the graph by the whole \({@abs(cc)@}^\circ\), but \(x\) is multiplied by \({@b@}\) inside the bracket. A translation carries the point of \(y = {@base@}\) at \(x = 0^\circ\), where the angle \({@b@}x\) is \(0^\circ\), to the point of the new graph where the angle \({@b@}x {@tc(cc)@}^\circ\) is \(0^\circ\). At your \(x = {@ans1@}^\circ\) that angle is \({@nice(b*ans1+cc)@}^\circ\).

Right size, wrong direction. A translation carries the point of \(y = {@base@}\) at \(x = 0^\circ\), where the angle \({@b@}x\) is \(0^\circ\), to the point of the new graph where the angle \({@b@}x {@tc(cc)@}^\circ\) is \(0^\circ\). At your \(x = {@ans1@}^\circ\) that angle is \({@nice(b*ans1+cc)@}^\circ\).

Check both the size and the direction of the shift. A translation carries the point of \(y = {@base@}\) at \(x = 0^\circ\), where the angle \({@b@}x\) is \(0^\circ\), to the point of the new graph where the angle \({@b@}x {@tc(cc)@}^\circ\) is \(0^\circ\). At your \(x = {@ans1@}^\circ\) that angle is \({@nice(b*ans1+cc)@}^\circ\).

falsefeedback.text: A translation carries the point of \(y = {@base@}\) at \(x = 0^\circ\), where the angle \({@b@}x\) is \(0^\circ\), to the point of the new graph where the angle \({@b@}x {@tc(cc)@}^\circ\) is \(0^\circ\). At your \(x = {@ans1@}^\circ\) that angle is \({@nice(b*ans1+cc)@}^\circ\). Take the \({@b@}\) out of the bracket as a factor to see the shift.

truefeedback.text: Your vector moves every point {@downup@} by \({@abs(d)@}\). Compare the two equations: is each \(y\)-value of the new graph larger or smaller than before?

falsefeedback.text: Your vector changes every \(y\)-value by \({@ans2@}\). Compare the two equations: what is added to every \(y\)-value of \(y = {@base@}\)?
